questions.prompt: Write \\(7-3i\\) in the form \\(a+bi\\) by naming \\(a\\) and \\(b\\).
questions.answer:
In standard form \\(a+bi\\), compare \\(7-3i\\) with \\(a+bi\\).
The real coefficient is \\(a=7\\).
The coefficient of \\(i\\) is \\(b=-3\\).

questions.prompt: What property of the imaginary unit \\(i\\) is used to simplify powers of \\(i\\)?
questions.answer:
The defining property is \\(i^2=-1\\).
For example, \\(i^3=i^2i=-i\\), so powers are simplified by replacing every \\(i^2\\) with \\(-1\\).

questions.prompt: Identify the real part and imaginary coefficient of \\(-5+8i\\).
questions.answer:
A complex number \\(z=a+bi\\) has real part \\(a\\) and imaginary coefficient \\(b\\).
For \\(-5+8i\\), \\(a=-5\\) and \\(b=8\\).

questions.prompt: Rewrite \\(4+i\\sqrt{11}\\) as \\(a+bi\\), then state \\(a\\) and \\(b\\).
questions.answer:
The term multiplying \\(i\\) is \\(\\sqrt{11}\\), so \\(4+i\\sqrt{11}=4+\\sqrt{11}i\\).
Thus \\(a=4\\) and \\(b=\\sqrt{11}\\).

questions.prompt: Simplify \\(6+4i^2\\) into standard complex form.
Simplify \\(3i^2-2i+9\\) into standard form.
questions.answer:
Replace \\(i^2\\) by \\(-1\\):
\\(3i^2-2i+9=3(-1)-2i+9\\).
Combine real terms: \\(-3+9=6\\).
So the standard form is \\(6-2i\\).

questions.prompt: A point in the complex plane has coordinates \\((-2,5)\\). Write the corresponding complex number.
questions.answer:
The horizontal coordinate is the real part and the vertical coordinate is the imaginary coefficient.
So \\((-2,5)\\) corresponds to \\(-2+5i\\).

questions.prompt: A complex number has real part \\(0\\) and imaginary coefficient \\(-6\\). Write it in standard form and describe its position in the complex plane.
questions.answer:
Standard form is \\(0+(-6)i=-6i\\).
Its real part is zero, so it lies on the imaginary axis, 6 units below the origin.

Compare \\(a+bi\\) with \\(12-7i\\).
Therefore \\(a=12\\) and \\(b=-7\\).

questions.prompt: Find real numbers \\(a\\) and \\(b\\) if \\((a-2)+(b+3)i=5-4i\\).
questions.answer:
Match real and imaginary parts separately.
Real parts: \\(a-2=5\\), so \\(a=7\\).
Imaginary coefficients: \\(b+3=-4\\), so \\(b=-7\\).

questions.prompt: Explain why \\(x^2+1=0\\) has no real solution but has complex solutions.
questions.answer:
The equation gives \\(x^2=-1\\).
No real square equals \\(-1\\), so there is no real solution.
In the complex numbers, \\(i^2=-1\\), so \\(x=i\\) works. Also \\((-i)^2=i^2=-1\\).
The complex solutions are \\(x=\\pm i\\).

questions.prompt: Show that \\(2+0i\\) and \\(2\\) represent the same complex number, then state its imaginary coefficient.
questions.answer:
A real number can be written as a complex number with zero imaginary coefficient.
Thus \\(2=2+0i\\).
The imaginary coefficient is \\(0\\), not \\(i\\).

questions.prompt: Find real \\(p\\) and \\(q\\) if \\((p+q)+(p-q)i=10+2i\\).
questions.answer:
Match components.
Real part: \\(p+q=10\\).
Imaginary coefficient: \\(p-q=2\\).
Add the equations: \\(2p=12\\), so \\(p=6\\).
Then \\(6+q=10\\), so \\(q=4\\).

questions.prompt: Find \\(t\\) if the complex number \\((t^2-9)+(t-3)i\\) is equal to \\(0\\).
questions.answer:
The zero complex number is \\(0+0i\\), so both parts must be zero.
Imaginary coefficient: \\(t-3=0\\), so \\(t=3\\).
Check the real part: \\(t^2-9=3^2-9=0\\).
Therefore \\(t=3\\).

questions.prompt: For what real values of \\(t\\) is \\((t^2-4)+(t+2)i\\) purely imaginary?
questions.answer:
Purely imaginary means the real part is zero.
Set \\(t^2-4=0\\).
Factor: \\((t-2)(t+2)=0\\), so \\(t=2\\) or \\(t=-2\\).
The number may be \\(4i\\) or \\(0\\); both have zero real part.

questions.prompt: For what real values of \\(t\\) is \\((t-1)+(t^2-1)i\\) a real number?
questions.answer:
A complex number is real when its imaginary coefficient is zero.
Set \\(t^2-1=0\\).
Then \\((t-1)(t+1)=0\\), so \\(t=1\\) or \\(t=-1\\).
The real parts are \\(0\\) and \\(-2\\), both allowed.

questions.prompt: Find all real \\(t\\) for which \\((t^2-1)+(t^2+t-2)i=0\\).
questions.answer:
Both components must be zero.
Real part: \\(t^2-1=0\\), so \\(t=1\\) or \\(t=-1\\).
Imaginary coefficient: \\(t^2+t-2=(t+2)(t-1)=0\\), so \\(t=-2\\) or \\(t=1\\).
The common value is \\(t=1\\).

questions.prompt: A learner says \\(\\operatorname{Im}(4-9i)=-9i\\). Diagnose the error and give the correct value.
questions.answer:
The imaginary part function returns the real coefficient of \\(i\\), not the whole imaginary term.
For \\(4-9i\\), the coefficient multiplying \\(i\\) is \\(-9\\).
So \\(\\operatorname{Im}(4-9i)=-9\\), not \\(-9i\\).

questions.prompt: Prove from standard form that if \\(a+bi=c+di\\), then \\(a=c\\) and \\(b=d\\).
questions.answer:
Subtract the two complex numbers: \\((a-c)+(b-d)i=0\\).
The zero complex number is \\(0+0i\\).
A point is at the origin only when its horizontal and vertical coordinates are both zero.
Thus \\(a-c=0\\) and \\(b-d=0\\), so \\(a=c\\) and \\(b=d\\).

questions.prompt: A complex number is both real and purely imaginary. What must it be? Justify using \\(a+bi\\).
questions.answer:
Let the number be \\(a+bi\\).
If it is real, then \\(b=0\\).
If it is purely imaginary with no real component, then \\(a=0\\).
Both conditions together give \\(a=0\\) and \\(b=0\\), so the number is \\(0\\).
